statement: All $180$ students in a grade were asked whether they play a school sport and whether they play a musical instrument. $$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & \text{Instrument} & \text{No instrument} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Sport} & 28 & 62 & 90 \\ \text{No sport} & 37 & 53 & 90 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 65 & 115 & 180 \end{array}$$ One of these students is chosen at random. What is the probability that the student plays an instrument and does NOT play a sport?

choices.misconception: I used everyone who plays an instrument, 65 out of 180, and ignored the condition about not playing a sport.
I divided 37 by the 90 students who play no sport, which answers a different question, given no sport, than the one asked.
I divided 37 by the 65 instrument players, which is the probability given an instrument, not out of all 180 students.

hints: The student is chosen from all $180$ students, so $180$ goes in the denominator.
Find the one cell where Instrument meets No sport.
That cell holds $37$ students, so the probability is $37$ out of $180$.

solutions.reliable: The student is chosen from all $180$ students. The cell for instrument and no sport has $37$ students, so the probability is $\dfrac{37}{180}$.
